steps.message:
`routes/users.js:6` is the only place — `userId: u.id` in the `GET /users` map. A one-character-class edit, but it's a response field name, so the consequence lands outside the lines I'd touch.

Per `README.md:3-5`, `GET /users` has three consumers — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and the README states field names are part of the contract, with changes going through a versioned endpoint. Renaming in place breaks any consumer reading `userId`, and the iOS clients and the partner export can't be redeployed in step with the API.

I haven't made the change. How do you want to handle it?

questions.question: Renaming userId to user_id in GET /users is a breaking contract change for the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export. How should I proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the same response. Consistency is available immediately to new consumers, nothing breaks, and userId can be dropped once the iOS and partner-export clients have migrated. Additive, reversible.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Keep /users as-is and add a versioned variant (e.g. /v2/users) that returns user_id. Follows the process the README already documents, but is more than a field rename -- a design choice, so I'd brainstorm it with you first.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Change userId to user_id in the existing response, exactly as asked. Fastest and cleanest, but breaks the three documented consumers until each is updated. Choose this if those consumers are already handled or the contract note is stale.
